result.overall: The Minister's application for judicial review is allowed because the Board member granted an extension of time to appeal without a reasonable explanation for delay or consideration of prejudice to the Minister.

themes.name: Extension of Time Criteria
themes.summary: The decision turns on whether the Board properly applied the criteria for granting an extension of time to appeal under s. 83(1) of the CPP.

themes.name: Reasonableness of Delay Explanation
themes.summary: The adequacy and credibility of the respondent's explanation for a seven-year delay is central to the outcome.

themes.name: Prejudice to the Minister
themes.summary: The Board failed to consider whether granting the extension would prejudice the Minister, which is a required factor.

themes.name: Procedural Fairness and Ex Parte Decision
themes.summary: The Board made its decision ex parte, without notice to or submissions from the Minister, raising fairness concerns.

arguments.claim: The Board member erred in granting an extension of time and leave to appeal after seven and a half years.
arguments.quote: the member erred in extending the time for bringing the appeal.

arguments.claim: The Board failed to consider the required criteria for an extension of time, including explanation for delay and prejudice to the Minister.
arguments.authority: Grewal v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration)
arguments.quote: the following criteria must be considered and weighed

arguments.claim: Extension of time and leave to appeal granted without reasons or submissions from the Minister.
arguments.quote: No reasons were provided. Further, the decision was taken ex parte, without notice to or submissions from the Minister.

arguments.claim: Delay was due to depression, marital problems, raising young children, and lack of understanding of the process.
arguments.quote: her reasons do not hold up to scrutiny.

holdings.statement: The Board member erred in granting an extension of time for appeal without a reasonable explanation for delay or consideration of prejudice.
holdings.quote: the member erred in extending the time for bringing the appeal

holdings.statement: The criteria for extension of time are: (1) continuing intention to pursue, (2) arguable case, (3) reasonable explanation for delay, (4) no prejudice to the other party.
holdings.quote: the following criteria must be considered and weighed

holdings.statement: No need to decide the standard of review since the decision fails on any standard.
holdings.quote: I do not need to reach a conclusion on the appropriate standard since I am satisfied that, on any standard of review, the decision should not stand.

holdings.statement: The decision is set aside and the matter is referred back to a different Board member for re-determination in accordance with these reasons.
holdings.quote: The decision under review will be set aside and the matter referred back to the Board for re-determination, having regard to these reasons, by a different member of the Board.

rebuttals.point: Respondent's delay was due to depression, marital problems, young children, and lack of understanding.
rebuttals.court_answer: The court found these reasons unsupported by the evidence and inconsistent with the record.
rebuttals.quote: her reasons do not hold up to scrutiny.

rebuttals.point: Board can grant extensions as a matter of right.
rebuttals.court_answer: The court held extensions are not a matter of right and must be based on principled criteria.
rebuttals.quote: An application for an extension of time...should not be granted as a matter of right, but should be subjected to a principled approach by the Board.

authorities.authority: Grewal v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1985] 2 F.C. 263 (F.C.A.)
authorities.why: Established the four criteria for extension of time, which the court adopted for CPP appeals.
authorities.quote: Jurisprudence relied on by the Minister...has established that the following criteria must be considered and weighed:

authorities.authority: Baksa v. Neis (c.o.b. Brookside Transport), [2002] F.C.J. No. 832
authorities.why: Cited as authority for the four criteria for extension of time.
authorities.quote: Jurisprudence relied on by the Minister...has established that the following criteria must be considered and weighed:

authorities.why: Cited regarding standard of review, but not decided.
authorities.quote: The Applicant submits that...I should apply a standard of review of reasonableness simpliciter (Callihoo v. Canada...)

authorities.why: Statutory basis for time limits and extensions for appeals.
authorities.quote: The statutory limitation of the time for bringing an appeal...is set out in s. 83(1) of the CPP

authorities.why: Analogized to the CPP provision for extension of time.
authorities.quote: The situation faced by a member of the Board...is analogous to that before a judge of the Federal Court in considering an extension of time...

left_open.issue: Whether the first two criteria (continuing intention and arguable case) were met.
left_open.reason: The court assumed, without deciding, that these criteria were satisfied.
left_open.quote: I am prepared to assume, without deciding, that the first two criteria have been met.

left_open.issue: Whether the Board must adopt procedures to ensure Minister's submissions on extension applications.
left_open.reason: The court declined to require procedural changes, deferring to the Board's control over its own procedures.
left_open.quote: I recognize that the Board is the master of its own procedures and, therefore, decline to require the Board to implement procedures that would address these shortcomings.
